utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good morning, Madam Registrar. Would you call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case IT-05-88-T, the Prosecutor versus Vujadin Popovic, et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Merci, Madam. I notice that all the accused are here. And from the Defence teams I notice the absence of Ms. Nikolic, Mr. Josse. That's all. And present for the Prosecution is Mr. McCloskey and Mr. Thayer. Mr. McCloskey and Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The witness is also here. We'll soon start with the continuation of your testimony. Good morning to you in the meantime. Mr. Krgovic, I understand you wish to address the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. In keeping with the decision of the Trial Chamber of the 26th of May, 2008, the Prosecutor and all sides to the proceedings are duty-bound at the moment when the witness starts testifying and takes the oath to submit documents that they would be using during cross-examination. General Gvero's Defence has observed that the Prosecution has not complied with this decision. We have addressed the Trial Chamber in writing asking for everybody to comply with this decision. Mr. Thayer submitted his documents for the last witness only when the examination was finished and for this witness we have still not received any documents. This has a great bearing on the cross-examination. Yesterday, for example, the documents arrived late to the Defence and that's why some questions were not raised on cross-examination. So what we are asking for everybody to do is to comply with the decision. That was the case during the Prosecution case. In case any Defence team was late disclosing documents and notifying the Prosecution what would be used, the Prosecution reacted. And I repeat, the moment this witness starts testifying and takes the oath, we would like to be given notification of all the documents that will be used during the examination of this said witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think this is an old story. We have debated this in the past and I think there are two categories of documents that one could speak of. The ones that are anticipated, and the ones that cannot be anticipated and the need for which arise in the course of the examination-in-chief. But anyway, I don't know who is going to address this? Yes, Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. President. Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning, everyone. I'll address it simply since I'm sitting here at this moment. It is really, frankly, a stunning argument to hear from my friends. They've asked us about it informally, we've told them what our position and our position is simple. We had an agreement with our friends that lasted for two years during the Prosecution case. That agreement was unanimous with respect to the Popovic team the agreement was withdrawn to some degree when Ms. Condon left but we had an agreement that we have discussed in Court on the record to which my friends made no objection, no qualification when this issue was raised before upon a complaint from the Popovic team. This is just shocking that we are hearing this now when they know what they agreed to. It's on the record. We've been abiding by that agreement. We specifically, as part of that agreement, agreed that the Defence could turn over their documents for cross upon the conclusion of the direct examination at the beginning of the cross-examination with the specific understanding that that agreement would hold during the Defence case. That was the understanding and it was unanimous and it was observed for two years. It doesn't take a rocket scientist to understand why we would agree to that. That was the consideration.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Stop. I think this is a matter that you should meet and discuss around the table again, once and for all. And we will abide by whatever decision you arrive. You all know that we have all along tried to avoid to intervene ourselves in these matters and we have left you entirely to come to an agreement, fully confident that you are perfectly capable of doing so. So let's not use more sitting time and go straight to the witness. Yes, Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Mr. President, just for of the record, the last discussion we had on this, on the record, was at transcript page 12141, May 29th of last year.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. So good morning, again, Mr. Jevdevic. Mr. Ostojic will continue with his examination-in-chief -- oh, Mr. Nikolic, sorry. Mr. Nikolic will continue with his examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Good morning. Good morning to everybody in the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Jevdevic.

utterances.speaker: MARINKO JEVDEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yesterday we left it off with a topic that we almost completed. It was about the effort of the administration of the security and intelligence service and on how to eliminate paramilitary formations. I'll have just a couple of more questions about that then I'll move on. Were there any other situations in which the military police was tasked with eliminating the work of paramilitary formations in some other regions and if that was the case, could you please tell us where and when that was the case?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO JEVDEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In the Sarajevo Romanija Corps. To be more precise, the paramilitary formation in question was the formation Brneta [phoen] in Ilidza up there. This is where the military police participated in the arrest of these individuals and their bringing in and placing under the control of the Army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Can you give us some more details of that paramilitary unit in Ilidza. Whose unit was it, who were the rogue individuals? Were they under somebody else's command or influence?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO JEVDEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were not under the command of the Army Republika Srpska, so we had received an order and Commander Malinic went with us. They were mostly volunteers from Serbia, I believe.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Very well, then. Tell me, please, until the end of the war, were there any other problems with those paramilitary formations? Were they finally eradicated and was their influence finally eradicated?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO JEVDEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After these two cases, we did not have any more problems with paramilitary formations in the Bratunac Brigade and Sarajevo Romanija Corps down there at Ilidza.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Now, I'm going to show you a document, 2D530. Can this please be brought up in e-court. We have a draft version of translation into English. Could you please look at the document just briefly. Read it and then we will comment on the document together. Can the document please be scrolled up to show the bottom of the page. Thank you. Can I continue?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO JEVDEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: The document was issued by the Main Staff. The date is 19 October 1995. Could you please just briefly tell me about the contents and the essence of this document?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO JEVDEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is an order which was issued by the Main Staff and it also applies to the 65th Protection Motorised Regiment which was our unit and the order was to remove such formations and other groups from the territory, as well as individuals who were not under command of the Army Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: In your opinion, does this mean that the problem was not completely resolved and that not all paramilitary formations were eliminated before this document was issued, what would you say?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO JEVDEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that that indeed is the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In the course of your testimony yesterday, you told us how the military police, headed by yourself, completed the job concerning paramilitaries in Bratunac and that you were also assisted by Colonel Beara during that operation. How often did you have an occasion to see Colonel Beara in the course of the war, of course?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO JEVDEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mostly saw him around the Main Staff or in the Main Staff itself. We would go there quite often. We were mostly engaged in providing security for the Main Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: I'm asking you this because I would like to draw some conclusions. After such a long time, would you be able to give us the description of his appearance, the way he looked at the time?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO JEVDEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Colonel Beara at the time was tall, heavily built, he had greying hair, he sported spectacles.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: And what was his military posture and attitude towards his subordinates, towards you, the military policemen?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO JEVDEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was rather strict, and he expected us to behave as soldiers. And this is exactly how he behaved, as a soldier. He demanded discipline from us.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Very well, thank you. Let's move on to something else now. Where were you when the operation around Srebrenica was taking place?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO JEVDEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the time I was with one part of my company in the vicinity of Sarajevo. To be more precise, I was in Treskavica.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Was that due to some combat activities or were you just performing your regular police duties there?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO JEVDEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time, there were combat activities in the area of Odjadjel [phoen] and also in the area of Umcani. I was in Kijevo with one part of my unit prepared for those actions.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: How long did you stay in the Treskavica sector, can you give us a time period?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO JEVDEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that it was on the 14th of July, 1995, when we left.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Where did you go on the 14th of July?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO JEVDEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 14th of July, I left for Nova Kasaba. I returned to my unit with two of my soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: And why did you return bearing in mind that there was combat going on at Treskavica, had the combat stopped or was there any other reason that required your presence in the unit?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO JEVDEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Combat had temporarily stopped. With my unit I was in Kijevo far behind the line and I went to Nova Kasaba because I had learned that one part of the troops were supposed to come back for regular leave and I was going to relieve them with some of my men, to replace those that were on leave.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: When you arrived in Nova Kasaba, who did you find there? Could you describe the situation as you saw it on the day when you arrived, and when was it, what time of day was it when you arrived in Nova Kasaba?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO JEVDEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I arrived on the 14th of July in the afternoon hours. And in the barracks I found the battalion commander Major Malinic. Troops were in the state of readiness, performing regular duties and jobs around the barracks.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: You joined them, didn't you, and what else did you do on that day? Did you have any conversations with Commander Malinic, did he brief you on the situation, did he update you on what had happened while you were absent?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO JEVDEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was updated in a conversation with Major Malinic. He told me what had happened the day before. There was fighting in that area of Kasaba and the surrounding hills. He gave me a task to take 12 soldiers and provide security for the barracks, to be prepared to intervene because fighting was still going on.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: So did you take the task, where did you go?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO JEVDEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I took the task. And there were not that many men. We were in the state of readiness.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: On that day did you scour the ground looking for any remaining groups in view of the fact that fighting had taken place the previous days?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO JEVDEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not on the 14th, but I did go to scour the terrain on the 15th.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Did anything significant happen during your mission, and was there anything that merited conversation with your commander? Was there anything that you had to inform your commander about?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO JEVDEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I took 14 soldiers towards the -- and I went towards the hill above Kasaba. We had information that a family, a Serb family lived in the village above Kasaba and that they resided there permanently. According to the information that we had, there was a strong likelihood that some Muslim units had had paid them regular visits inquiring about our positions and we had received an order to pay a visit to that family. We did that, and we found an elderly woman up there. She told us that a group had arrived on that very morning and that other groups came very frequently. She even gave food to one of those groups. I don't know what food she gave them, but in any case she did feed them. She did not want to go back to Nova Kasaba with us. And we proceeded further following some information according to which in the surrounding hills at a water source and in some swimming pools there was a large quantity of hidden weapons. We were still trying to find those hidden weapons. As we were looking for them, we came to a forest path, a road. We noticed that there were several soldiers from Srebrenica there. They were enemy soldiers who had committed suicide.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Just a moment, please. How do you know that they committed suicide? Can you give us some more details? As I'm listening to your answer I can conclude that they were dead, did you see bodies?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO JEVDEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they were dead. There was quite a number of bodies there. They were lying scattered on that forest trail in smaller groups. There was not a very long trail and we knew from the intelligence that we received earlier that there had been instances of self-destructions and this is what we found. I got interested in that and I took a few soldiers to inspect the situation, and as I say, they were scattered all along the road and we could establish that they had killed either each other or they committed suicide with bombs. And we could conclude that judging by the wounds that they had inflicted upon themselves with those grenades. We left the scene very quickly because of the stench. The bodies had already started decomposing by then.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Mr. Jevdevic, I will now put another document to you. Could we please see 2D233. We also have a draft English translation. Could we please have it distributed to the Trial Chamber. Could you please take a look at the document and then we shall analyse it. Would you please look at paragraph 4. That is the paragraph that is important for us. Can we proceed?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO JEVDEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: This is an official note composed by the ministry of the interior police station in Srebrenica on the 26th of August, 2003. You have read it now. Would you please now tell us what this is about?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO JEVDEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It has to do with this person describing the things similar to what I had seen but worse. I didn't come across such people out in the field. I only came across such people who were killing. I didn't see anybody who had hung themselves.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Based on this statement given by Sinahid [phoen] has -- it seems that he was one of those in the column who had managed to reach Tuzla, to break through to Tuzla?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO JEVDEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: So this is his description of events taking place that you witnessed yourself or, rather, you saw the consequences of those events; right?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO JEVDEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: When you came back on that day after touring the terrain, when you came back to Nova Kasaba, did you inform the commander about everything that you had seen?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO JEVDEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I informed him about what I had seen out in the field and he confirmed to me that there was some information that in the village of Jelah, that there was some intelligence information indicating that a group had been found there in that village, a group of people that had committed a mass suicide.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: All right. When you arrived on the 14th in the afternoon and then on the 15th you spent the entire day Nova Kasaba, were there any prisoners?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO JEVDEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were no prisoners.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: In that period of time on the 14th in the afternoon and on the 15th, did you see -- or, rather, did you see specifically Ljubisa Beara who was chief of security in Nova Kasaba and in that area?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO JEVDEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not see Ljubisa Beara in the Kasaba area.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Who did you find there when you came back from touring the terrain?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO JEVDEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Upon my return from the terrain on the 15th when I came back to the barracks at the school in Nova Kasaba where we were housed, I saw that there were two vehicles parked, two vehicles of UNPROFOR. Those were two Mercedes jeeps.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: And did that make you inquire about what was going on?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO JEVDEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I asked my friends from the military police and the crime technicians and they told me that those were two jeeps that the UFOR commander from Potocari had given them as a gift and he personally brought them there and gave the keys to Major Malinic allegedly due to very proper behaviour of our soldiers because they had spent there sometime.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: And what was the fate of those vehicles, did they remain with you or did you transfer them to the security administration or to the Main Staff or to somebody else?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO JEVDEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. One remained with us and was used by the military police. And later on it was rotated and was used as our vehicle when we were carrying out our assignments. As for the other one, I don't know where it ended up. I think that it was sent to the police in Han Pijesak.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Please tell me, while you were there on the 14th and the 15th in Nova Kasaba, did you find there or did you see there any of those UN soldiers?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO JEVDEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: All right. Thank you?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: That concludes my examination Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you Mr. Nikolic. Madam Fauveau, he is also your witness. Sorry, Mr. Petrusic. It seems you are going to examine the witness. Please go ahead and introduce yourself.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a moment, Your Honour, Mr. President. First of all, good morning, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Witness. My name is Nenad Petrusic and on behalf of the Defence team of General Miletic, I will be putting questions to you. At the very outset, I would like to clarify certain matters, namely, that you on page 9, line 3, said to Mr. Nikolic that you had information that in the hills in the water sources and swimming pools there was some weaponry. Please explain to me what swimming pools were you referring to?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO JEVDEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't referring to any swimming pools. I was referring to reservoirs of drinking water that the local residents used.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Did you find any weaponry there?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO JEVDEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: And next to those dead bodies that you came across, did you find any weaponry there, next to them?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO JEVDEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they were in uniforms. And based on everything I had seen, they were members of the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina. They had belts, ammunition on them, and some of them had rifles still on them.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Tell me, please, in July of 1995, did you have a rank?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO JEVDEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was second lieutenant.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: What about the unit that was under your command, was that the same unit that you had under your command back in 1992?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO JEVDEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in 1992 I was a platoon commander and now I was a commander of an anti-terrorist company.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: How long did you stay in Nova Kasaba, until what time?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO JEVDEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I left Nova Kasaba on the 17th in the morning hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Are you referring to the 17th of July, 1995?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO JEVDEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the 17th of July, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Who did you leave Nova Kasaba with, and pursuant to whose orders did you leave it?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO JEVDEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I left Nova Kasaba with the members of my unit, 14 of them. On the 17th in the morning at about 6.30, I set out towards Zepa pursuant to the order of General Savcic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Did General Savcic directly issue the order to you?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO JEVDEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, Commander Malinic conveyed to me the order of Savcic which I carried out subsequently.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Could you give us more details, what exactly did Major Malinic convey to you?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO JEVDEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 16th in the evening, late in the evening, Major Malinic called me and told me, "There's a message for you from General Savcic, for you and your package to set out at dawn towards the Zepa area."

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: You knew what that code stood for, your "package" or your "parcel," you knew what that meant?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO JEVDEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I knew. It referred to my soldiers. We used that term frequently.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Which road did you take from Nova Kasaba to Zepa, and how did you travel?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO JEVDEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I set out in a vehicle, in a terrain vehicle. It was a Pinzgauer, an open vehicle. I set out towards Nova Kasaba, Han Pijesak and the village of Godjenje.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: And on that road or around that road did you observe that there were any combat activities, was there any fighting taking place between Nova Kasaba and Han Pijesak?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO JEVDEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not notice anything except for police checkpoints that were stepped up and moving towards the village of Godjenje and to the forward command post, I did not notice anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Let us go back for a moment to Nova Kasaba. Those 10 or 12 people of yours, when did they reach Nova Kasaba?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO JEVDEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Some of them arrived on the 13th and some on the 14th. Because in Zvornik they waited for the road to Nova Kasaba to be opened; it had been closed. So they arrived there before me.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: And when you set out from Nova Kasaba, how many people remained in the military police battalion under the command of Major Malinic? When I say people I'm referring to soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MARINKO JEVDEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He remained there with some 20 to 30 people, approximately.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And that military police battalion, do you remember what its strength was? How many men it had in its numbers?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO JEVDEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it was 500-odd people in that military police battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Do you know, do you remember, where were they deployed at that time?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO JEVDEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A part of the battalion was in Treskavica, another part, or rather, a platoon of my company -- before me one had been in Zepa. Then a company of armoured vehicles was also in the Zepa area and the barracks in Han Pijesak, because prior to that we had some combat activity around the Main Staff and they remained there on alert. A lot of people were wounded in the activities around Treskavica. Over 100 people were wounded and were put out of action.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Mr. Jevdevic, when Major Malinic told you that you should go to Zepa did he provide you with the specific location where you should report and whom you should report to and did you know that, the identity of the person that you were to report to?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO JEVDEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, he told me that the forward command post of General Savcic was located in the village of Godjenje [Realtime transcript read in error "Gorazde"] and it was quite natural that I should report to him. He was the commander of the protective regiment, so I was reporting to him.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Well, this is a little bit leading question, but I hope there will be no objections from the Prosecution. So on the 17th you arrived in Godjenje [Realtime transcript read in error "Gorazde"]?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO JEVDEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right I arrived at the forward command post at Godjenje.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Who did you found there at the IKM, the forward command post?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO JEVDEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I encountered several people at the forward command post, General Mladic, Major Jevdevic, and after that I reported to General Savcic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Major Jevdevic is your brother, is that not right?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO JEVDEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he is my brother.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Did you remain there at the forward command post at all?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO JEVDEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We remained there for a very short period of time.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Did you receive any orders from anyone at the forward command post?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO JEVDEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, General Mladic asked us to go with the troops towards the village of Ljubomislje. Then I spoke to him, I said I have the remains of my unit, a platoon deployed around Brezova Ravan and that I should report there and that General Savcic was waiting for me, and he approved it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Madam Fauveau warns me that at page 15, line 23, and page 16, line 3 through 5, instead of IKM Godjenje it says IKM Gorazde, so I would like that to be corrected. We'll do it through a question. Mr. Jevdevic, are we talking about the IKM forward command post at Godjenje?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO JEVDEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, at Godjenje.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: And what was the reason why you stopped at that forward command post?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO JEVDEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I knew that my brother, Major Jevdevic, Milenko Jevdevic, was deployed in that area. I recognised his vehicle. The vehicle that he was using that was a communications vehicle. And I wanted to see my brother. That's all.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: So finally you encountered General Savcic; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO JEVDEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I reported to General Savcic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Did you have in your unit any chemical weapons?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO JEVDEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we did have some chemical rounds.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Could you please explain what kind of weapons are we talking about for the benefit of the Trial Chamber?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO JEVDEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, some of my soldiers had been issued those hand grenades, AG1 hand grenades and they contained tear gas. They are used by all the police forces, the police -- civilian police and military police uses it and it is establishment equipment.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Well, and those hand grenades, are they used for riot control?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO JEVDEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, precisely.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: And to use this kind of chemical weapons, would you have to have some protective equipment, gas masks, something like that?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO JEVDEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we were all supposed to have protective masks in order to be able to use the hand grenades.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: And did you have such masks?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO JEVDEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time we didn't have those masks.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: And do you know whether chemical weapons were used, any kind of chemical weapons, in combat operations around Zepa?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO JEVDEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know anything about any use of chemical weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now, I would like to move on to something else. Could you please tell us something about those combat operations, or rather, how you received the tasks from General Savcic, the combat operations and who issued tasks to your unit? So could you please tell us what tasks did you get from him?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO JEVDEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The task was to join a platoon led by Lieutenant Stojan Maksimovic . He had been in the field there for a long time. He was in the area of Brezova Ravan and he sent me there and the same day I reached Lieutenant Stojan Maksimovic in the area of Brezova Ravan. I asked him to give me intelligence about their trenches and we were getting ready to launch an attack. And we attempted an attack the same evening. But we were unsuccessful and had to pull back to the initial positions.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: So you are talking about the 17th of July?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO JEVDEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's all this is happening on the 17th of July.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: And could you please tell us, were you in contact with Stojan Maksimovic or with Savcic, the Maksimovic that you were mentioning?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO JEVDEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we were in contact using radios, we had Motorolas.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Were you part of the communications system of the Drina Corps, were you in contact with them?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO JEVDEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I was not in their communication system.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: So General Savcic was the only person issuing orders to you?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO JEVDEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he did that on our frequency using communications equipment.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: After that first meeting with General Mladic sometime in the morning of the 17th, did you see him again on the 17th, during the day?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO JEVDEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Let's go on. On the 18th, on the 18th of July, how did combat operations proceed, did you get any new tasks and what did your command do vis-a-vis you, what were you doing in other words?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO JEVDEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 18th I was at the same axis and I continued with the same task. And in the morning of the 18th, I launched an attack with my unit along the Brezova Ravan axis.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Do you know that there is a point or a checkpoint at Brezova Ravan and to our knowledge it was supposed to be an UNPROFOR checkpoint or point?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO JEVDEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, General Savcic told me about that and he said that this point had been taken over by the Muslim army from Zepa, that they had taken the UNPROFOR soldiers to Zepa and they had been using this UNPROFOR point as their stronghold.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: And what kind of weapons were the Muslim forces from the Zepa Brigade using in offering or rather, in engaging your forces, can you say that, do you have any knowledge of that?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO JEVDEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, apart from light infantry weapons, light machine guns, I actually didn't know what they were using. But they were using some larger calibre weapons, I didn't know what it was. Up until the time when we actually managed to take an APC, that was on the 18th, that was an UNPROFOR battalion APC, it was located there at this UNPROFOR point and it was used by the enemy side to engage us.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: And that was on the 18th?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO JEVDEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, on the 18th in the morning. That's when we took Brezova Ravan.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Could we please have 5D1112 put on our screens. Mr. Jevdevic, could you please focus on item 2 of this document originating from the Drina Corps. Could you please read it and when you've read it we can perhaps comment on it. On the 19th of July did you really take the village of Vratar and approaches to the village of Borak and reached -- or in other words, reached the approach routes to the village of Borak as indicated in this report.

utterances.speaker: MARINKO JEVDEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 19th of July, I and my unit took the village of Vratar which was on our axis. I'm not familiar with Borak, we were not heading in that direction.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Do you have any knowledge that in that part of the theatre or rather, in the fighting around Zepa that in addition to the units of the 65th Regiment, your unit and this other unit that was commanded by General Savcic that there were other units from Drina Corps deployed there?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO JEVDEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there were other units of the Drina Corps. There was the battalion to the left of me from the Bratunac Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Do you know that there were elements of the units of the 2nd Romanija Brigade deployed there and elements of the Birac Brigade?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO JEVDEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they were there too.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Could you please look at item 3 now. On the 19th of July, did you at any point receive an order, and if so from whom, to cease combat operations?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO JEVDEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 19th of July as we were taking the village of Vratar, we received an order from General Mladic via radio and it indicated clearly to all units to stop fighting and to remain where they are, to remain at the lines that they had reached.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: So this was a direct order from General Mladic?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO JEVDEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, a direct order from General Mladic that we received on the radio.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: In the course of the proofing for this testimony, you indicated where the village of Vratar was, but could you please tell us now, from the point that you reached when General Mladic issued this order to cease all combat operation, did you have a line of vision to Zepa?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO JEVDEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you could see the whole of the village of Zepa from that location quite clearly.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: And do you know where at the time, we are talking about the 19th of July, the Muslim armed formations were, members of the 285 Zepa Brigade?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO JEVDEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I could infer that on the basis of the fighting that was going on in the direction of the Zepa mountain that was on the opposite side from where I was, so I could conclude that they were on the opposite side.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: And on that day, the 19th, the truce, did it apply to all units participating in combat?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO JEVDEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it applied to all. That was the order, or at least I received that order.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: From then on for as long as you were deployed in the area, did you receive any order to continue fighting?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO JEVDEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not receive any further orders about any combat.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: From that point, could you see what was going on in Zepa at that moment in the town itself?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO JEVDEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We could see civilians' movements around Zepa. Above the centre of the village of Zepa there is a village called Cavcici and there I could observe a large number of civilians.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: The way I understand you, the large number of civilians came from Cavcici?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO JEVDEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Cavcici, Purcici --

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Just a moment, hold on, please. Where did those civilians arrive from?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO JEVDEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They arrived from the direction of the Zlovrh, and then they came to the villages of Purcici and Cavcici, and --

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: According to your information at the time when the civilian population was entering Zepa from the surrounding villages, the troops of either the Drina Corps or the 65th Regiment, did they enter the village of Zepa or did they remain on the lines reached up to then?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO JEVDEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time none of our troops, or any troops for that matter, entered the village of Zepa.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: And you did not take the village of Zepa in military terms?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO JEVDEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's true, we did not take Zepa.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Can we now see document number P3015. Please look at the document, Mr. Jevdevic. On the 20th of July when this document was issued, according to your information, in addition to the 20 or 30 soldiers that he had in Nova Kasaba, did Major Malinic have at his disposal another military police battalion?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO JEVDEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he did not have at his disposal any military police battalions. He had the troops that he had. The troops that remained.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Just a moment, please, bear with me. How long did you stay in the territory of Zepa, up to what time?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO JEVDEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't tell you exactly, but it could have been either the 25th or the 26th of July.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Did you see any movements of civilians from that little town?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO JEVDEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Civilians kept on coming in larger numbers to the village of Zepa.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: After the ceasefire was declared on the 19th, from that day up to the 25th of July when you left, did you receive any combat orders?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO JEVDEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we did not receive any orders for combat. We kept maintaining the lines reached.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: And during that period of time there was the time of ceasefire, there was no combat going on anywhere?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO JEVDEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, nothing from our positions, but there was some sporadic fire in the direction of the road towards Zup [phoen].

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: And that sporadic fire, when did this start, did it start after the 20th, after the 21st, after what date did that start?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO JEVDEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 25th or on the 26th it was still going on at a somewhat higher intensity.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: And do you know which units participated in these activities, in the exchange of fire?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO JEVDEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that those were the units of the Drina Corps which were on our left. A flank towards Zlovrh and Zepska Koliba.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: On the one side you had troops of the Drina Corps and on the other side you had Zepa Brigade; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO JEVDEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Do you know whether Zoran Malinic came to Zepa at any one time?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO JEVDEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't know, I didn't see him. If he had arrived, I would have seen him.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: In the area where you were deployed up to 25 or 26, did you see civilians being moved out of Zepa, did you see any civilian buses or any means of transportation for the civilians?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO JEVDEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On that day I saw buses leaving for Zepa and on that day civilians started being transported out of Zepa.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: What day was that?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO JEVDEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was on the last day of my stay. I left Zepa sector on the day when civilians started being moved out.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: From the Zepa sector, where did you go?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO JEVDEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Pursuant to General Savcic's order, I went to the Han Pogled Pass since on that day there was combat around the Zepa mountain and Zlovrh. Some of the armed Muslim troops broke through our lines and proceeded on the Zepa-Kladanj road. My task was to intercept them in the area in the pass on the road leading from Han Pijesak towards Vlasenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: And how long did you stay there?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO JEVDEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We did not stay long because I received the order to return to the Han Pijesak barracks, and there I received an order to form a column and go towards Han Pijesak, Kasaba and to proceed further towards Krajina.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: So the unit that was with you proceeded towards Krajina?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO JEVDEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, on the same day.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Jevdevic, I have no further questions for you. Mr. President, I have completed my examination in chief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Petrusic. Mr. Zivanovic, do you have cross-examination for this witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: No, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, sir. Mr. Bourgon, do you have a cross-examination for this witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: No cross-examination of this witness, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Bourgon. Mr. Lazarevic?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: No cross, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Krgovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have a few questions but I still have not received the Prosecutor's list of documents that they will be using with this witness and that's why I'm asking the Trial Chamber to allow me to raise any questions that may be raised by the Prosecution during their cross-examination and that might have a bearing on my client.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We'll have a break now and discuss it with Mr. Thayer. We are not going to change the procedure, Mr. Krgovic, that we have adopted. 25 minutes. --- Break taken at 10.23 a.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krgovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I just wanted to inform the Trial Chamber that during the break we have spoken within the Prosecutor and that we will try and reach an agreement on the timing of the disclosure of documents. And Mr. Thayer has kindly informed me that he will not be using any documents with this witness and I believe that from now on we will be able to reach a consensus between the two sides.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you for that, both of you. Let's proceed with your questions, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Jevdevic. My name is Dragan Krgovic and on behalf of General Gvero Defence team, I'll have some questions for you. Mr. Jevdevic, in answering my friend's questions you described your stay in Zepa in July 1995. When you were withdrawing from Zepa, you took the road from Zepa towards Rogatica when you were leaving that sector; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO JEVDEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I went in the direction of Rogatica.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: On the road from Zepa towards Rogatica when you were withdrawing, either on the 25th or the 26th, were there any checkpoints manned either by the military or the police between Zepa and Rogatica?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO JEVDEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were no checkpoints at all manned either by the police or the military.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And in the other direction as you were entering Zepa, when you arrived in Zepa on the 17th of July, did you encounter any military police checkpoints from the point where you left until you arrived at the IKM?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO JEVDEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not notice any checkpoints on arriving there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Could you describe the road between Rogatica and Zepa or Brezova Ravan were you were billeted. Was it an asphalt road or dirt road?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO JEVDEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was an asphalt road between Rogatica and Budeta [phoen]. And at Sjeverska, I turned left towards Zepa.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And the road there is a dirt road?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO JEVDEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I have no further questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Krgovic. Mr. Haynes, do you have a cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: No, thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Thank you Mr. President. I can confirm that as a result of hearing how the evidence came in, we have no documents that we intend to use. We did not need to send out our exhibit list.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, good morning to you. My name is Nelson Thayer. I'll be asking you some questions on behalf of the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MARINKO JEVDEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And I actually only have one question for you. You testified that your recollection is that from the period of the ceasefire on the 19th of July onwards during your time in Zepa, your recollection is there was no further fighting; correct?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO JEVDEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the 19th of July, 1995, in the area where I was moving around the village of Vratar, we did not open fire and fire was not open at us. We did not engage in combat.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And to your knowledge from that period of the 19th on, were other VRS units, be they 2nd Romanija Motorised Brigade units, units from the Zvornik Brigade or other units including your own that were elsewhere than Vratar, did you understand that there was fighting engaged in by those units?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO JEVDEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was fighting in the areas of Zepa mountain and Zlovrh because the Muslim armed forces were trying to break through the frontlines there. That was across the mountain from where I was. I was on the other side.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, just to follow up with my last question for you, sir, with respect specifically to Brezova Ravan, that feature, there has been testimony before this Trial Chamber from various witnesses, both Muslim as well as from General Savcic that the fighting for that feature continued for approximately ten days, in his recollection, from 15 July to on or about the 24th or 25th of July. And for anyone who is interested, that is at the transcript page 15333, 13 September 2007. Now, sir, is it possible that your recollection that Brezova Ravan was taken on the 18th mistaken, given the testimony that this Chamber has heard from including General Savcic who was very specific about the dates and the length of time it took to take that feature, that you are mistaken in your recollection?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO JEVDEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I arrived in the Zepa theatre of war on the 17th. And the UNPROFOR checkpoint at Brezova Ravan is what we call Brezova Ravan feature although the whole sector extends to the village of Ljubomislje. That's where Savcic had his unit because we had a battalion or, rather, a company from Han Pijesak which consisted of the population and that unit was on the strength of the protection regiment. And my platoon commander was in the Zepa frontline throughout all that time; I joined him on the 17th. And on the 18th in the morning, we carried out a breakthrough towards the Brezova Ravan checkpoint where the EUFOR checkpoint was. On the 18th of July, we took the checkpoint at Brezova Ravan, I wouldn't be able to give you the precise measurements of the Brezova Ravan territory, the entire territory.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Sir, I have no further questions, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Thayer. Is there re-examination, Mr. Nikolic?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour. None.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Petrusic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No re-examination, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Jevdevic, we have finished with you. We don't have any further questions for you which means you are free to go. Our staff will assist you. On behalf of the Trial Chamber I wish to thank you for having come over and on behalf of everyone present, I wish you a safe journey back home.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Nikolic, documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Documents from our 65 ter list that we used 2D233 [Realtime transcript read in error "2D333" 2D529 and 2D530. They have been submitted to the Prosecution and I believe that they are also ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, any objections?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: None, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Other Defence teams, any objections? None. They are so admitted. Mr. Petrusic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have one document which is 5D1112, that we would tender.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Any objections.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: No, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, just one correction. In the transcript on page 30, line 12, the number is 2D333 and it should be 2D233.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you for that correction. Any objections from the other Defence teams? None. So your documents are also admitted. Mr. Thayer, I suppose you don't have any documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: No, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Which that concludes the testimony of Mr. Jevdevic. And we come to the next witness, which I understand is the expert.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: That's correct, Mr. President. Dr. Debra Komar is our next witness. We would request a five- to ten-minute break so that Dr. Komar can set up her computer laptop. It did fall coming in through security this morning but it seems as if it's okay. We'd ask the assistance of the technician just so that can be up and running, if it it's acceptable with the Court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. We'll have a short break then. Thank you. As soon as you are ready, please inform us. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: We'll do so. --- Break taken at 11.10 a.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So are we all set, Mr. Ostojic?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: We are, Mr. President. Thank you again very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: How shall we call you, Professor Komar, Dr. Komar?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Dr. Komar is fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good morning to you. You are very much welcome to this Tribunal. I'm the Presiding Judge. To my right I have Judge Kwon, Judge Stole, and on my left I have Judge Kim Prost. You've been summoned as an expert witness by the Defence team for Colonel Beara in this case. And before you start giving evidence, our rules require that you make a solemn declaration which would be equivalent to an oath in some jurisdictions that in the course of your testimony you will be speaking the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth. Text has been made available, please read it out aloud and that will be your solemn undertaking with us.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Doctor. Please make yourself comfortable. Mr. Ostojic will go first. I don't anticipate your testimony to finish today. So I assume that you will be here with us again tomorrow. Mr. Ostojic.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Dr. Komar. As you know, my name is John Ostojic and I represent Mr. Ljubisa Beara. Can you please for the record state your full name.

utterances.speaker: DEBRA KOMAR
utterances.text: Debra, D-e-b-r-a, Komar, K-o-m-a-r.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Dr. Komar, since we do have the transcript translated in several different languages, I am going to just tell you but it's really a reminder to myself that we should try to pause before I either put another question to you or before you commence providing us with an answer. So if you could just accommodate me to the extent that you can I'll try to do the same, obviously. Thank you. Dr. Komar, could you please share with us your brief background history, where were you born and what year, if I may ask that question.

utterances.speaker: DEBRA KOMAR
utterances.text: I'm a Canadian citizen, I was born in St. Katherine's, Ontario, Canada, in January of 1965.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Share with us, if you will, your education background starting with any bachelors or undergraduate studies that you had undertaken?

utterances.speaker: DEBRA KOMAR
utterances.text: From 1990 to 1994, I completed a bachelor of science at the university of Toronto in Toronto, Canada. From 1994 to 1996, I completed a masters of science in the department of anatomy and cellular biology at Queens University in Kingston, Ontario. In 1996 to 1999, I completed my PhD in the department of anthropology in forensic anthropology at the University of Alberta in Edmonton, Canada.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Would you be kind enough to tell us what is the study of forensic anthropology?

utterances.speaker: DEBRA KOMAR
utterances.text: The discipline of anthropology is the study of human beings. The forensic aspect of anthropology essentially takes the methods and theories that are part of our discipline specifically relating to issues such as archeology and physical anthropology and translates them into a medical/legal context, brings them into a court of law.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: How long have you been a forensic anthropologist?

utterances.speaker: DEBRA KOMAR
utterances.text: I began my training in 1990 and I've been practicing non-stop since.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Let's go over some of the experience that you have. I know you highlighted some of it in your curriculum vitae that we have marked as 2D533. And could you share with us, please, first and foremost, if you were ever involved in any exhumations in the area commonly referred to as Srebrenica resulting in events that unfolded there in 1995?

utterances.speaker: DEBRA KOMAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And can you tell us who contacted you to be involved in that exhumation process?

utterances.speaker: DEBRA KOMAR
utterances.text: I was involved in two separate occasions. The first occasion was in 1999 when I was contacted by Dr. Brenda Kennedy who was the director of the Physicians for Human Rights organisation that had been contracted to be doing inter-entity exhumations with the commissions, the Bosnian commission, the Serbian commission, the Croat commission in the Srebrenica area. And I was a forensic anthropologist in 1999 with Physicians for Human Rights. My area of responsibility included the Srebrenica area. In 2001, I was contacted by the International Commission on Missing Persons to hold a brief contract to assist with the joint exhumations in the Srebrenica area that were carried out jointly between the ICMP, the Missing Persons Commission, and the ICTY.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now, the exhumations that you conducted in 1999, did it have a name of a dig specifically?

utterances.speaker: DEBRA KOMAR
utterances.text: We were working with the Bosnian inter-entity commission responsible for recovering those individuals associated with Srebrenica that were not under the jurisdiction of ICTY. So the commission themselves were responsible for identifying and initiating the investigation. They provided us the information, the potential sites.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And can you just tell us what role specifically you played that exhumation in 1999?

utterances.speaker: DEBRA KOMAR
utterances.text: I would be responsible for the field recovery of those remains and on several occasions I was also responsible for the analysis of remains associated with Srebrenica in what is known as the PIP morgue in Podrinje.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Similarly if I may ask you with respect to your involvement in 2001, can you share with us what your responsibilities were in connection with that exhumation?

utterances.speaker: DEBRA KOMAR
utterances.text: The ICTY provide both the investigator, the criminalist who was responsible for the scene and a senior archeologist who was responsible for documenting the overall grave and scene itself. ICMP agreed to provide technical support in terms of osteology and physical anthropology, so I was responsible essentially for the delineation, examination and removal of human remains from within the grave context.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Can you describe for us what osteology is or the discipline of osteology ?

utterances.speaker: DEBRA KOMAR
utterances.text: Osteology is study of human remains through the hard tissues of the body, specifically bone, teeth.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And were you -- were these digs, did they have a name that you were involved in 2001, because obviously from the review of your curriculum vitae we know or should know that you were involved in an exhumation identified as Cincari 7 and Liplje 4, I believe; correct?

utterances.speaker: DEBRA KOMAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And that's the name of the two exhumations that you conducted in 2001?

utterances.speaker: DEBRA KOMAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now, doctor, we'll come back to this in a little bit. I just want to get a little better feel for your experience in exhumations. Have you conducted other exhumations throughout your career?

utterances.speaker: DEBRA KOMAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Can you share with us or highlight some of those, please.

utterances.speaker: DEBRA KOMAR
utterances.text: In the international realm and on a mass scale, I have worked in -- I was part of the team that was responsible and answered to the regime crimes liaison which was a joint Iraqi High Tribunal and the US Department of Justice that was responsible for the investigation of genocide and war crimes charges against Saddam Hussein and 14 of his co-defendants. That was in August through November of 2004 in Iraq. Additionally, I have worked in Kosovo for the United Nations as part of the UNMIK mission to Kosovo. Specifically, I worked for the OSCE as an identification project officer. I was stationed at the ICTY morgue facility in Rahovec and was responsible for the identification and repatriation of victims of the Kosovo conflict.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you for that. If I may just follow up, can you tell us what the OSCE is and also for the sake of brevity, can you also tell us what an identification project officer is?

utterances.speaker: DEBRA KOMAR
utterances.text: OSCE is the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe which is -- I believe is one of the branches or pillars of the United Nations. Identification project officer essentially was to be -- or what we were tasked with was the independent review of the human remains specifically to answer the question of personal identity. So we weren't responsible for the evaluating trauma or other aspects, we were tasked solely with attempting to put names back to decedents.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Were you one of many who were involved in this or were you in any supervisory capacity or the director of that identification process?

utterances.speaker: DEBRA KOMAR
utterances.text: There were four of us, all told.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Share with me, if you will, a little bit about your employment history, and specifically were you ever involved in working with ICMP?

utterances.speaker: DEBRA KOMAR
utterances.text: I worked as a contract forensic anthropologist for ICMP in 2001.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And can you share with us what your job duties and responsibilities were with ICMP in 2001 as a contract forensic anthropologist?

utterances.speaker: DEBRA KOMAR
utterances.text: They were conducting a joint experiment with the ICTY at the time to provide additional technical and expert support in the field in terms of dealing with what were understood to be large secondary mass graves that to that point had not been excavated by the ICTY. So while the ICTY had the, I suppose, jurisdictional authority over the site and were responsible for the overall site itself, the ICMP was assisting in terms of dealing with the human remains themselves.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And at that time, if I may, were you familiar with the standard procedures and protocols that the ICMP implemented in connection with any such excavations?

utterances.speaker: DEBRA KOMAR
utterances.text: I understand what standard operating procedures were, at that time in that circumstance I was not provided with SOPs.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And we'll go through some of the SOPs during your testimony, so thank you for that. That's why I asked. Let me talk about memberships and professional organizations or associations. Are you affiliated with any such associations or organisations?

utterances.speaker: DEBRA KOMAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Can you just list a couple for me?

utterances.speaker: DEBRA KOMAR
utterances.text: I am a fellow of the forensic anthropology/physical anthropology section of the American Academy of Forensic Sciences which means essentially I hold a senior or advisory leadership rank. I'm also a full member of the Canadian Association of Forensic Sciences.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And most recently you were an associate professor at the department of anthropology at the University of New Mexico in Albuquerque, New Mexico, United States; is that accurate?

utterances.speaker: DEBRA KOMAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Share with us if you have ever published any articles, books or periodicals in connection with the discipline of anthropology and specifically forensic anthropology?

utterances.speaker: DEBRA KOMAR
utterances.text: I'm the senior or sole author of two books relating to forensic anthropology. The first is a senior graduate textbook entitled Forensic Anthropology: Contemporary theory and practice, which I co-authored with distinguished professor Dr. Jane Buikstra from the Arizona State University. The second is a sole volume that I'm the author of entitled, Forensic investigation of genocide, victim selection, identification, and identity, published by Charles C. Thomas. I am the author, either the first author or the sole author of 22 articles in print and three under review for peer-reviewed journals all addressing the issue of either forensic anthropology or specifically international investigations of genocide.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] That's obviously --

utterances.speaker: DEBRA KOMAR
utterances.text: I can no longer hear anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I was shuffling some papers and trying to be courteous, turned the mike off. Obviously, that's reflected in part in your curriculum vitae as we identified 2D533; correct?

utterances.speaker: DEBRA KOMAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I know that you also highlight other sections in your CV that we won't go into but certainly you've received several, if not many, academic awards and distinctions. I won't embarrass you to go through that but that's an updated CV that we have in front of you. If I can perhaps just have the Court or with the Court's permission have the usher just pull up 2D533 which is Dr. Komar's curriculum vitae. Doctor, looking at what was attached, I believe, to your report as an appendix with your name in the top centre and if you look at the screen in front of you, my question is simple, is this a current curriculum vitae reflecting not only your educational experience and accomplishments, but other work that you've been involved in including publishing and et cetera?

utterances.speaker: DEBRA KOMAR
utterances.text: While it's an accurate reflection of my status in February of 2008, I believe is the date on it, I would suggest that there have been additions and revisions since that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. Let me just follow up with that so we have a clear record. Is there anything of significance that you would like to add and if so, please do?

utterances.speaker: DEBRA KOMAR
utterances.text: The positions listed as current positions I have resigned from as of three weeks ago. So the associate professorship, I have resigned my tenured professorship at the University of New Mexico and I have resigned my position as the forensic anthropologist for the office of the medical investigator.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: You've piqued our curiosity, I'm sure. What will you be doing in the next few months, if I can ...

utterances.speaker: DEBRA KOMAR
utterances.text: Well, this seems to be taking some of my time.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I apologise for that. I know that you were scheduled last week, thank you again for agreeing to come a little later, I apologise for that. Are you going on another contracted engagement as an anthropologist?

utterances.speaker: DEBRA KOMAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Can you share with us, if it's not confidential, as to where you may be heading towards in the next several months?

utterances.speaker: DEBRA KOMAR
utterances.text: My next round of research will be conducted in Rwanda relating to the genocide from 1994. That's in association with completing a funded external grant contract that I need to complete.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I think we've spent an adequate time on your curriculum vitae. Thank you for that. What I'd like, Dr. Komar, to ask you is, when -- you were asked to review certain materials from our Defence team, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DEBRA KOMAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And we'll go through the contact, et cetera. Can you tell us first and foremost, was there a task assigned to you in connection with the materials that we were requesting you to review?

utterances.speaker: DEBRA KOMAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Share with us what that task was.

utterances.speaker: DEBRA KOMAR
utterances.text: Originally I was approached by Mr. Christopher Meek representing the Defence team for Beara. I was asked to review the available scientific evidence that was being presented to the Court at that time. Specifically looking at the validity of the methodology primarily relating, at that time, to the question of establishing what is known as MNI or the minimum number of individuals.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Did at any time during your review of certain documents which we'll list out in a moment, were you asked to review the scientific material or evidence that was presented by the Prosecution to analyse in addition to their methodology, the analysis and the conclusions that were reached by the various scientists that they brought forward?

utterances.speaker: DEBRA KOMAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: So in addition to methodology, the task was to review and give us an objective opinion as to the methodology and analysis and conclusions of the scientific evidence that the Prosecution was offering specifically in connection with MNI; correct?

utterances.speaker: DEBRA KOMAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Although we know it and we use it commonly, forgive me for asking you this, MNI stands for?

utterances.speaker: DEBRA KOMAR
utterances.text: The minimum number of individuals.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Is that an anthropological term or just simply a scientific term?

utterances.speaker: DEBRA KOMAR
utterances.text: It's derived from the anthropological literature, specifically the archeological literature.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: In connection with the task that was requested, can you tell me at any point did any of the Defence counsel, including myself, of course, the investigators, ask you to skew your report in one way or another?

utterances.speaker: DEBRA KOMAR
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. And in fact, Doctor, you wouldn't in any event; correct?

utterances.speaker: DEBRA KOMAR
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now, let me ask you with respect to prior testimony that you may have been engaged in during your professional career. Have you testified in court before?

utterances.speaker: DEBRA KOMAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And just give us a ballpark estimate as to how many times you've testified in court?

utterances.speaker: DEBRA KOMAR
utterances.text: In a major capacity, probably about a dozen or so times in both US and Canada.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Did you testify in the Saddam Hussein trial?

utterances.speaker: DEBRA KOMAR
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: At that trial there was limited scientific evidence; correct?

utterances.speaker: DEBRA KOMAR
utterances.text: It was restricted to very small portion of one day.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now, have you ever testified for the Office of the Prosecutor, not at the ICTY but in any capacity as an expert witness?

utterances.speaker: DEBRA KOMAR
utterances.text: I have only previously testified on behalf of the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: So have you ever testified, although I think I know the answer based on that answer that you provided, have you ever testified for a Defence in any criminal proceedings in connection with forensic anthropology or any of the fields that you are experienced and educated in?

utterances.speaker: DEBRA KOMAR
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: So this would be the first case?

utterances.speaker: DEBRA KOMAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Dr. Komar, can you briefly share with us the material that you reviewed in connection with determining or formulating any opinions that you may have in connection with this case, and for the Court and counsel, if we can have 2D534 brought up to the screen, please. Doctor, while this is coming up on the screen, I do have a couple of other personal questions, if you don't mind, not really personal but -- did you know Mr. Christopher Meek prior to his contacting you in connection with assisting us in this case?

utterances.speaker: DEBRA KOMAR
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Did you know myself at any time prior to meeting last week and exchanging a couple of brief e-mails with respect to scheduling?

utterances.speaker: DEBRA KOMAR
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Have you ever worked for either of us?

utterances.speaker: DEBRA KOMAR
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Or anyone else on our Defence team?

utterances.speaker: DEBRA KOMAR
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Counsel and witness are kindly asked to make pauses between questions and answers.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I apologise it was just a brief area.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now, we have in front of us, I believe, 2D534, which -- if we could look at the last page of that document or the last two pages, I believe. Then, Doctor, once you have that document in front of you, can you just tell us generally what this document is. It's attached again, I think, to your report which has your curriculum vitae attached to it as well.

utterances.speaker: DEBRA KOMAR
utterances.text: As of February of this year, this was a list of exhibits that I had been sent and had reviewed for the purposes of this trial.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And who generated this list?

utterances.speaker: DEBRA KOMAR
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And this is over a course of a certain period of time that we, the Defence for Mr. Beara, were providing you with additional information; correct?

utterances.speaker: DEBRA KOMAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
